title: My child's blood lead level is elevated - what do I do and how do I find the source?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.basis: One CDC policy document, based on NHANES. It states what the number is and what it is not.

answerHtml: CDC's blood lead reference value is 3.5 µg/dL for children aged 1 to 5 years, equal to the level at or above which 2.5 percent of those children fall. CDC says it is not a toxicity threshold, that no safe blood lead level in children exists, and that follow-up testing to confirm the level is recommended. This corpus does not contain a verified checklist for finding the source in a home, so no search protocol is invented here.

sections.heading: What CDC states about the number
sections.html:
The saved MMWR page says venous blood is less likely to be contaminated than a skin prick. It says whether a result at or above 3.5 µg/dL triggers medical or environmental follow-up depends on jurisdictional laws, regulations, and resources. It points clinicians to CDC's recommended actions based on blood lead level. This site does not reprint a treatment plan. doi:10.15585/mmwr.mm7043a4.

In NHANES 2017 to 2018, children aged 1 to 5 years had a blood lead geometric mean of 0.670 µg/dL and a 95th percentile of 2.02 µg/dL (n=629), read from the saved CDC table. That row is population description, not a diagnosis.

sections.heading: What chelation did and did not do
sections.html: In children with blood lead of 20 to 44 µg/dL, succimer lowered blood lead and did not improve cognition. That trial is graded on the DMSA page. It is not a set of instructions.

buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
